newsitem.title: ST VINCENT AND THE GRENADINES: American couple acquitted of murder on St.Vincent.
newsitem.headline: American couple acquitted of murder on St.Vincent.

text.p: An American couple whose round-the-world sailing voyage turned into a nightmare when they were charged with murder were acquitted on Friday by a court in the Caribbean nation of St.Vincent and the Grenadines.

James and Penelia Fletcher, of Huntingdon, West Virginia, embraced each other in the dock as Judge Dunbar Cenac upheld defence submissions they had no case to answer in the murder of water taxi-operator Jerome "Jolly" Joseph last October.
They had faced death by hanging if found guilty.
"I have found no evidence against the accused in the course of the prosecution's case and I am therefore directing you to return a verdict of not guilty," Cenac told the 12-member jury.
The Fletchers had been charged with the murder in October of Joseph, a 30-year-old water-taxi operator on the tiny island of Bequia.

Outside the court after he and his wife walked free, James Fletcher told a crowd of reporters, well-wishers and sight-seers, "The trial was carried out with the finest tradition of jurisprudence. Justice has been served."
Fletcher, 50, retired president of a mining equipment company, and his 35-year-old wife, known as Penny, arrived in St.Vincent last August while sailing their yacht "Carefree" around the world.
Joseph ferried rich tourists from their boats to Bequia. On the night of Oct. 6 he picked up the Fletchers from a late dinner. Three days later his bullet-riddled body was fished out of the sea.
The Fletchers were arrested on Oct. 30 and held in separate jails.
The case gained notoriety as gossip about the Fletchers' lifestyle circulated. During the trial, Penelia Fletcher said her husband was an alcoholic and that Joseph would look after her.
The Fletchers also charged that they were victimised by corrupt officials, and some U.S. commentators questioned whether they would get a fair trial on the island.
